sessions.title: Proverbs Wisdom Themes
sessions.theme: Match Proverbs excerpts to wisdom themes.

rounds.title: Proverbs 1:7
rounds.verseTextShort: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction.
rounds.teachingNote: Reverence for the Lord is the starting point of biblical wisdom.

rounds.title: Proverbs 2:6
rounds.verseTextShort: For the Lord giveth wisdom: out of his mouth cometh knowledge and understanding.
rounds.teachingNote: Wisdom is received from the Lord.

rounds.title: Proverbs 3:5-6
rounds.verseTextShort: Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding.
rounds.teachingNote: The passage warns against depending only on one's own understanding.

rounds.title: Proverbs 4:7
rounds.verseTextShort: Wisdom is the principal thing; therefore get wisdom: and with all thy getting get understanding.
rounds.teachingNote: Wisdom and understanding are presented as things to pursue.

rounds.title: Proverbs 4:23
rounds.verseTextShort: Keep thy heart with all diligence; for out of it are the issues of life.
rounds.teachingNote: The heart must be guarded because it shapes life.

rounds.title: Proverbs 6:6
rounds.verseTextShort: Go to the ant, thou sluggard; consider her ways, and be wise.
rounds.teachingNote: The proverb rebukes laziness by pointing to steady work.

rounds.title: Proverbs 10:12
rounds.verseTextShort: Hatred stirreth up strifes: but love covereth all sins.
rounds.teachingNote: Love is contrasted with strife.

rounds.title: Proverbs 10:19
rounds.verseTextShort: In the multitude of words there wanteth not sin: but he that refraineth his lips is wise.
rounds.teachingNote: Wisdom includes restraint in speech.

rounds.title: Proverbs 11:14
rounds.verseTextShort: Where no counsel is, the people fall: but in the multitude of counsellors there is safety.
rounds.teachingNote: Many counsellors provide safety.

rounds.title: Proverbs 11:25
rounds.verseTextShort: The liberal soul shall be made fat: and he that watereth shall be watered also himself.
rounds.teachingNote: Generosity is pictured as fruitful refreshment.

rounds.title: Proverbs 12:22
rounds.verseTextShort: Lying lips are abomination to the Lord: but they that deal truly are his delight.
rounds.teachingNote: Truthfulness is pleasing to the Lord.

rounds.title: Proverbs 13:20
rounds.verseTextShort: He that walketh with wise men shall be wise: but a companion of fools shall be destroyed.
rounds.teachingNote: Companions shape a person's path.

rounds.title: Proverbs 14:12
rounds.verseTextShort: There is a way which seemeth right unto a man, but the end thereof are the ways of death.
rounds.teachingNote: A path can appear right while leading to death.

rounds.title: Proverbs 14:29
rounds.verseTextShort: He that is slow to wrath is of great understanding: but he that is hasty of spirit exalteth folly.
rounds.teachingNote: Patience with anger is tied to understanding.

rounds.title: Proverbs 15:1
rounds.verseTextShort: A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger.
rounds.teachingNote: Words can calm or inflame anger.

rounds.title: Proverbs 15:22
rounds.verseTextShort: Without counsel purposes are disappointed: but in the multitude of counsellors they are established.
rounds.teachingNote: Plans are strengthened by counsel.

rounds.title: Proverbs 16:18
rounds.verseTextShort: Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.
rounds.teachingNote: Pride is shown as a warning sign before ruin.

rounds.title: Proverbs 16:24
rounds.verseTextShort: Pleasant words are as an honeycomb, sweet to the soul, and health to the bones.
rounds.teachingNote: Gracious words bring sweetness and health.

rounds.title: Proverbs 17:17
rounds.verseTextShort: A friend loveth at all times, and a brother is born for adversity.
rounds.teachingNote: Faithful friendship is steady in adversity.

rounds.title: Proverbs 18:10
rounds.verseTextShort: The name of the Lord is a strong tower: the righteous runneth into it, and is safe.
rounds.teachingNote: The righteous find safety in the Lord's name.

rounds.title: Proverbs 18:21
rounds.verseTextShort: Death and life are in the power of the tongue: and they that love it shall eat the fruit thereof.
rounds.teachingNote: The tongue carries serious power.

rounds.title: Proverbs 19:17
rounds.verseTextShort: He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto the Lord; and that which he hath given will he pay him again.
rounds.teachingNote: Mercy to the poor is treated as service to the Lord.

rounds.title: Proverbs 22:1
rounds.verseTextShort: A good name is rather to be chosen than great riches, and loving favour rather than silver and gold.
rounds.teachingNote: Reputation is valued above wealth.

rounds.title: Proverbs 22:6
rounds.verseTextShort: Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.
rounds.teachingNote: The proverb speaks to parental formation and instruction.

rounds.title: Proverbs 27:17
rounds.verseTextShort: Iron sharpeneth iron; so a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend.
rounds.teachingNote: Wise friendship sharpens and strengthens.
